summary: A is materially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the exact required API and uses multipartbody.NewFile, while B introduces prohibited APIs, association fields, multipart machinery, and retry-layer changes.
reasons: A preserves the required Upload signature with opts ...FilesOption; B replaces it with opts ...UploadFileOption, violating the exact API contract and changing option compatibility.
A directly reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile as required. B adds NewFileWithFields chiefly to support association fields that the contract explicitly forbids.

B expands scope substantially by changing Raw.Do replay semantics for all seekable request bodies, despite the contract prohibiting retry-machinery refactoring and requiring the convenience upload to solve replayability through buffering.

B adds seven association option APIs and documents them, directly conflicting with the instruction not to add association fields and to keep FilesOption behavior unchanged in Upload’s interface and routing path.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add's request, response, option, and error logic instead of routing the multipart body through Add, violating a central maintainability requirement.
Tests omit explicit validation and source-reader error cases.
The retry test counts requests but does not verify that each retried request received the complete multipart filename and content.
risks_b: Upload neither has the mandated signature nor routes through FilesService.Add.
The new association-option system and NewFileWithFields are prohibited scope expansion and duplicate existing option machinery.

The global seekable-body replay implementation mutates and reuses one seeker across attempts, broadening concurrency and lifecycle risk beyond this feature's needs—even though recorded gates passed it here—while changing Add and other Raw.Do behavior repository-wide in conflict with the frozen contract and its scope limits; comments and documentation further cement that unintended behavior change.
